column4: Hand-painted pixel art in the style of a 1990s DOS adventure game crossed with a Build-engine horror game: chunky visible pixels, a limited muted palette, slightly worn and grimy, no readable text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no border. A close-up straight on, at arm's length, seen from a little above: the top of a wrought-iron votive candle stand in a damp neglected Czech village chapel, the same black iron and dark red glass cups as the reference. Three stepped tiers of plain round dark red glass votive cups, five cups on every tier, evenly spaced in clean rows across the picture, each cup standing in its own iron ring, and in each cup you see down onto a stub of pale wax with a short black wick in the middle. None of them burning. Old wax run down the rims, soot on the glass. Behind the stand a dark damp plaster wall, flaking, with black mould and brown tide lines. Across the whole bottom fifth of the picture a broad dark oak ledge, worn and scorched by old wax: at its left end a small dented grey tin offering box with a coin slot in its lid and a little padlock, right beside it a chipped white enamel saucer with a few loose wooden matches with red heads. The rest of the ledge is bare. Even soft flat light all over, nothing in deep shadow, no flames, no hands, no people. Cold, musty, eerie, a Slavic PlayStation 1 horror game.
